• In 2017, the KES exchange rate against the USD
remained relatively stable, trading at a monthly
average of 102.9 to 103.9.
• It hit a monthly average high of 103.9 in July
following precautionary purchase in the run up to the
general elections as well as demand from sugar and
maize importers.
• 2018 is expected to have sufficient food supply.
• Fuel may be the only item giving pressure to the
Kenya Shilling in 2018.
